subject: Clarifications on DPA annex: PII provenance, subprocessors, and transfers
messages:
From: Sara Day <sara.day@innovamed.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@innovamed.com, procure@innovamed.com
Date: 2026-11-10T08:23:00Z
Subject: Clarifications on DPA annex and PII handling for InnoVamed integration

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Before we can move to procurement/tech onboarding, our legal and security teams asked us to confirm a few items in the DPA annex. I've attached our short SSQ with focused questions. Could you confirm the following at a high level so we can decide whether to request redlines?

- Which Redwood subprocessors will have access to customer PII (list and country of operation)?
- What elements of PII (raw text, identifiers, metadata) are stored persistently vs transiently in the inference pipeline?
- Where is the KMS key material held for hosted deployments serving EU customers (GCP KMS, customer-managed, HSM)?
- Do you provide a dataflow diagram showing handoffs between ingestion, caching, model inferencing, telemetry, and archival?
- Are there any cross-border transfers that would move unredacted PII outside the EU for hosted customers? If so, what safeguards are in place?

Attachments: innovamed_ssq.xlsx (limited set)

We'd appreciate a short written reply and — if helpful — a 30-min call with your security contact. Target timeline: procurement needs answers by Nov 16 to keep Q4 onboarding.

Best,
Sara
Sara Day
Head of Platform Integrations | InnoVamed
[sara.day@innovamed.com]
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Sara Day <sara.day@innovamed.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-10T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifications on DPA annex and PII handling for InnoVamed integration

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list and the SSQ. Quick responses below; happy to expand on any item or jump on a call. I've attached our current DPA draft with non-substantive redline notes (dpa_redline_v1.pdf) and a small PNG snapshot of the EU dataflow.

- Subprocessors: For hosted EU customers we rely on three categories: compute (GCP europe-west1), observability & logging (Datadog - EU region), and object-store archival (GCS - europe-west1). The full roster and country mapping is in the DPA annex we shared; we will include the same roster in the formal subprocessor disclosure during procurement.

- PII storage: Redwood's inference path is designed to minimize persistent storage of raw customer-provided prompt/response text in hosted mode. By default:
  * Transient: request prompt and immediate KV cache (evicted per TTL), model activations, and ephemeral logs used for debugging (redacted).
  * Persistent: customer-configured artifacts only — e.g., customer opt-in logs, long-term audit archives, or artifacts placed into archival buckets for compliance. We do not persist raw prompts for model training.

- KMS custody: For Redwood-hosted EU deployments we can offer two models:
  1) Redwood-managed GCP KMS (keys in europe-west1) for standard hosted customers;
  2) Customer-managed keys (BYOK) where the key is in the customer's GCP/AWS KMS or HSM and Redwood uses wrapped keys for runtime decryption.

- Dataflow diagram: a snapshot is attached (redwood-dataflow-infra-eu.png). It shows ingestion -> pre-processing -> KV cache -> model inferencer -> response; telemetry and traces are sampled and sent to Datadog EU; audit exports to customer GCS buckets are optional. Full editable diagram available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Xy-dataflow-innova

- Cross-border transfers: For customers who select EU-hosted capacity, we ensure compute and storage remain in EU regions; however, some support and control-plane functions (metadata, billing) may interact with US services. We document each transfer in the DPA and offer SCCs or SCC-equivalent clauses, and can restrict cross-border flows as an addendum for regulated customers.

Proposed next steps:
- We'll complete the SSQ with evidentiary links by Nov 13.
- If you need a KMS attestation or subprocessor evidence bundle, we can provide that within the procurement window.

Would Mon 11/15 or Tue 11/16 09:00-10:00 CET work for a quick sync with our security lead (Monica)?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

From: Sara Day <sara.day@innovamed.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@innovamed.com, procure@innovamed.com
Date: 2026-11-11T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifications on DPA annex and PII handling for InnoVamed integration

Thanks Jonas — that helps. A few follow-ups from the SSQ (inline where possible):

On Subprocessors:
- Could you provide a timestamped roster (CSV) with contractual start dates and country of processing for each subprocessor? We need that for our procurement intake.

On PII persistence:
- Please confirm whether any telemetry or debugging traces might include unredacted customer identifiers (user_id, email) and whether those are scrubbed before being sent to Datadog.

On KMS:
- If we choose customer-managed keys (BYOK), is there any requirement for key rotation cadence or supported HSM vendors?

On Cross-border transfers:
- We require explicit confirmation that EU-hosted inference will not transfer unredacted PII to US data centers under normal operation. Any exception path must be described.

Attachments: updated SSQ with a couple of marked questions (innovamed_ssq.xlsx)

Could Monica or Karthik prepare the roster and a short note on telemetry redaction before the call? Procurement needs the roster and DPA redline by Nov 16.

Best,
Sara
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sara Day <sara.day@innovamed.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-11T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarifications on DPA annex and PII handling for InnoVamed integration

Hi Sara — looping in Karthik (platform security) and following up with the deliverables we can provide this week. Inline responses and plan below.

- Subprocessor roster: we'll export a timestamped CSV that includes service, country, contractual start date, and purpose. Expect the file by EOD Nov 12. Provisional entries: compute:GCP europe-west1 (Netherlands), observability:Datadog EU (Germany), archive:GCS europe-west1 (Netherlands), monitoring:PagerDuty (EU tenancy), SSO:Okta (EU tenancy).

- Telemetry & traces: by default telemetry is sampled and PII is redacted before leaving the runtime. Karthik: can you confirm the fields we scrub and where code-level redaction occurs?

- BYOK: we support customer-managed KMS for GCP and AWS KMS. Key rotation cadence can be customer-controlled; we recommend a 90–365 day rotation policy depending on customer risk profile. Supported HSM vendors: Google Cloud HSM / AWS CloudHSM; for on-prem HSM we accept wrapped key import where compatible. We'll provide an attestation template for BYOK usage.

- Cross-border transfers: for EU-hosted capacity, default operation keeps inference compute and storage in EU. Control-plane metadata (billing IDs, non-sensitive job metrics) may cross borders for operations; we will provide an explicit exception list. No unredacted PII is transferred to US under normal operation. If you require contractual guarantees, we can add a clause restricting control-plane export and provide SCCs and an addendum.

Action items & timeline:
- Nov 12 EOD: timestamped subprocessor roster CSV (monica)
- Nov 13 EOD: completed SSQ answers with evidentiary links and redaction field list (karthik)
- Nov 15: 30-min sync with security/legal (suggested 09:00 CET)
- Nov 16: final DPA redline/acceptance target for procurement

I'll attach the roster CSV and a short telemetry-scrub summary after we run it past Karthik.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
